claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in the HEA is governed by retention of a fine dual-phase L12/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The retained L12/B2 lamellar microstructure supports homogeneous chromium distribution.
Homogeneous chromium availability enables robust passive-film repair.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 contains approximately 71% L12 and 29% B2 phases.
The B2 phase occurs as 2–3 µm lamellae containing nanoscale chromium-rich precipitates.
Hot-rolled DS2205 contains approximately 52% austenite and 48% ferrite.
After three rapid heating and quenching cycles to approximately 1100 °C, the HEA retains its dual-phase structure better than DS2205.
The stable HEA lamellar structure produces a more stable and smaller wear track.
DS2205 undergoes phase redistribution that undermines passive-film stability.
Film instability in DS2205 increases debris-assisted wear.
Temperature controls the competition between sliding-induced depassivation and thermally activated repassivation.
At approximately 50 °C, faster passive-film repair creates a low-shear polishing regime and minimizes wear.
At 25 °C, insufficient passive-film repair favors direct two-body abrasion.
At 100 °C, repeated formation and rupture of oxide or tribolayers increases third-body wear and corrosion.
Under identical testing, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will exhibit a lower coefficient of friction than DS2205.
Under identical testing, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will produce a smaller wear volume than DS2205.
Under identical testing, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will have a substantially lower tribocorrosion wear rate than DS2205.
The HEA performance advantage over DS2205 will be most pronounced at 50 °C.
Both alloys will show less combined degradation at 50 °C than at 25 °C or 100 °C.
The predicted behavior is limited to 25–100 °C, 5–15 N, 3–9 Hz, a 3.5 mm reciprocating stroke, an alumina counterbody, and deionized water.
